thread:
alex: heads up — after the smoothquant + mixed-kernel routing change on canary we saw NaNs show up in a subset of long-context requests (L>4k). p95 stable but p99 spikes and some streams produce Inf in KV cache :eyes:

maria: ugh. which model / kernel combo? do you have a minimal repro or logs?

alex: repro attached to the canary run (link): https://perf.internal/reports/17688 — happens with fp8-int8 mixed kernels when alpha is 0.5 and per-tensor scaling. logs show 'Inf detected in kv_cache layer=23' then subsequent tokens become NaN.

perf-bot: profiling snapshot:
```
2026-03-17T21:12:34Z canary/run/587
model: redwood-xxl-8k
kernel-order: [int4-opt, int8-quant, fp8-mixed, fp16]
alpha(smoothquant)=0.5
p50 latency: 28ms
p95 latency: 120ms
p99 latency: 560ms (regressed +2.8x)
throughput (tokens/s): 540 -> 410 on canary
exception rate: 0.8% (NaN/Inf in kv cache)
```

jonathan: reproducer looks deterministic for a particular prefix distribution (lots of repeated tokens + positional wrap). suspect quant scale overflow on KV update path. might be per-channel vs per-tensor issue.

priya: quick mitigation: clamp KV writes and fallback to fp16 for layers that exceed scale threshold. we already have fallback hooks in kernel selector. can flip to prefer fp16 for layers where scale>2**10 or if smoothquant variance high.

maria: can we try lowering alpha (smoothquant) and switch to per-channel scales for attention projection matrices? that usually stabilizes extremes.

alex: tried alpha=0.3 + per-channel for proj_wq/wk, null repro for same inputs locally. but perf cost: token throughput dropped ~6% in the canary.

jonathan: tradeoff acceptable short term. need to root cause: is overflow happening during kv accumulation (add/mul) or during quant->dequant rounding?

qa-bot: attached trimmed logs from failing request:
```
[warning] layer23 kv_write: max_abs=1.3e5 scale=2.1e-4 -> quantized=int8 max=127 -> overflow on dequant: value 1.27e7 -> Inf after softmax
stack: kv_update -> attn_out_quant_dequant -> update_kv_store
```

priya: that max_abs looks suspicious — scale too small due to extreme embedding deltas. smoothquant may have pushed weights to smaller scales for some channels. per-channel prevents this collapse. also we need clipping on forward outputs before kv write.

alex: proposed quick patch:
- change kernel routing to prefer fp16 for layers with abs_scale_ratio > 1e4
- add saturating clamp at KV write: clamp(x, -CLIP, CLIP) where CLIP = 1e4 for now
- run scale-sweep job to recompute safe alpha per model and update recommendations

jonathan: implemented kernel-order override in runtime (flag: runtime.quant.force_fp16_threshold). testing now on canary2. added metrics to track "kv_clamp_hits" and "kernel_override_count".

perf-bot: canary2 results (after patch):
```
p95: 130ms (small regression)
p99: 210ms (huge improvement vs 560ms)
throughput: 480 tokens/s
kv_clamp_hits: 0.73% of requests
kernel_override_count: 12 layers across 3 hosts
exception rate: 0.02% (post-clamp)
```

maria: can we reduce clamp to 1e3 and rerun sweep? 1e4 feels ad-hoc. also we should compute per-model recommended CLIP and alpha via offline calibration (scale histogram).

priya: agreed. I'll run a scale-sweep that computes per-layer scale percentiles (50, 99, 999) and propose clamp=percentile_999 * 2. will also compute per-channel variance and suggest per-channel if variance>threshold.

alex: note: kernel override affects latency — we must exclude it for low-latency tiers. will gate by route policy. default for non-critical routes is safe-mode.

jonathan: next steps:
- priya run sweep and post artifact (calib manifest) -> assigned to priya
- maria validate that per-channel adaption doesn't break small models -> assigned to maria
- alex roll canary with clamp=1e3 if sweep suggests lower bound -> assigned to alex
- jonathan add unit tests for kv_clamp and a synthetic adversarial prefix test -> assigned to jonathan

infra-bot: created ticket INF-1243 and a canary rollout job: canary/quant-stability/176880.

maria: also add a regression test in our perf harness that runs long-prefix sequences and asserts no NaN in KV after 10k tokens.

alex: thanks. will keep thread updated. if anyone sees fresh NaNs ping me @alex. :bug: :shipit:
